headline: Highest risk is medium: ECC can write shared files and use MCP while emqx has broad network egress, creating plausible injection, leakage, and cascading-error paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can write files, use MCP, and read filesystem content; emqx exposes an HTTP API and broad egress. A plausible pairwise path is ECC-generated or user-supplied content being consumed by emqx workflows without provenance checks. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly observed, so uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF ECC output is copied into emqx-controlled prompts, configs, or API payloads without sanitization
IF emqx treats inbound text from ECC as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable any automatic ingestion of ECC-generated text into emqx workflows
Add a manual review step before passing ECC output to emqx
Restrict emqx API inputs to structured schemas only
Log provenance for any ECC-to-emqx handoff
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging across the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, learned skills, hooks, and security findings, and can read/write the filesystem; emqx handles IoT data and has broad network egress. If they share a workspace or files, sensitive ECC artifacts could flow into emqx outputs or outbound traffic. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this remains inferred but credible.
conditions: IF ECC and emqx share any filesystem, volume, or mounted workspace
IF emqx forwards file contents or payloads containing ECC artifacts to external endpoints
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different directories or volumes
Keep ECC secrets and session files out of any emqx-ingested path
Review outbound emqx payloads for accidental inclusion of ECC artifacts
Use least-privilege file permissions on shared hosts
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC has unrestricted filesystem write, git-state modification, subprocesses, and allowlisted network egress; emqx has broad network egress and HTTP API access. Their write surfaces overlap on shared mutable resources if co-located, but the profiles do not show a guaranteed shared directory or locking. That makes a real conflict plausible in default multi-agent setups, but not proven high.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository, directory, or mutable workspace
IF either agent writes to files or state that the other also edits without locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories to each agent
Avoid concurrent writes to the same git branch or config files
Serialize state-changing operations with a simple operator checklist
Snapshot shared files before agent runs
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional state updates

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC can produce security findings, documentation, and code, while emqx can act through HTTP APIs and broad egress. If emqx consumes ECC output as authoritative, a mistaken ECC result can cascade into outbound actions or misconfiguration. The profiles suggest an action-taking pathway, but no direct verification step is documented, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF emqx uses ECC-generated text, configs, or findings as authoritative input
IF emqx executes API calls or outbound actions based on ECC output without verification
mitigations: Require human approval before any emqx action based on ECC output
Compare ECC output against a second source before execution
Limit emqx to read-only mode for ECC-derived inputs
Record the exact ECC artifact used for each downstream action
requires-engineering: implement validation gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: ECC explicitly handles security findings, session data, and secrets-related settings, while emqx touches IoT data and has broad egress. A compliance issue is possible if regulated data is routed from ECC into emqx, but the profiles do not show a specific residency or certification mismatch. Because the pathway is only weakly evidenced, low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data from ECC is forwarded into emqx without a documented policy match
IF retention or logging settings differ for the same data class across the two agents
mitigations: Classify data before handing it from ECC to emqx
Avoid routing secrets or sensitive findings through emqx
Check retention settings on both agents
Document the allowed data classes for each agent
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
